findings.text: follow-on: the three except clauses now 'raise' for every subprocess.CalledProcessError, not only exit 255. The reference the plan cites (imas_codex/discovery/paths/scanner.py:210-226) re-raises only returncode 255 and records any other exit code as a per-path error, because those are permanent script failures rather than transient SSH drops. Here a non-255 script failure releases the batch's claims and retries up to max_ssh_retries on every pass instead of being recorded, and no test covers a non-255 exit. The change is not wrong for the plan's stated goal (a failed call must not become an empty result) but it is broader than 'raises on exit 255'.

justifications.durability: the guard is a control, not an assertion of intent: restoring the swallowed exception makes the 255 test fail (reproduced, EXIT=1), and the timeout and unparseable arms fail identically at base, so all three swallow sites are load-bearing. Residual risk is finding 3 (the scanner now raises on every CalledProcessError, not only 255, so a permanent non-255 script failure is retried up to max_ssh_retries each pass rather than recorded as a path error; no test covers a non-255 exit).
justifications.evidence: the head gate (8 passed, EXIT=0) is reproduced by an independent head arm that imported the reviewed tree's scanner, and a comparable base arm at 84e76711b (3 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1) closes the added-failure question at zero; the negative-control mutation is reproduced (255 test: 1 failed, EXIT=1). Gaps: the reviewed manifest carries empty baseline_suite/after_suite objects, its baseline.log header names revision=84e76711b although the run measured the head test file against the base package (that revision predates the test file), and the head test file's success-case mock was corrected in two later commits, so the first two test revisions were not green.
justifications.fit: the change adopts the exception-propagation idiom the spec cites from imas_codex/discovery/paths/scanner.py (raise for transient failures so the existing retry path runs), reuses the worker's existing claim-release block rather than adding a parallel path, tests are named by mechanism, commits carry conventional subjects with bodies, and no plan, sprint, ticket or author identifier appears in the code, tests or messages (checked).
justifications.goal_fidelity: the cause from the plan is reproduced at base (all three failure tests fail with paths marked {first:0,second:0}) and refuted at head; the fix raises on 255, timeout and unparseable output, the worker releases claims without marking, and the not_a_directory control still records 0 files; the plan's four done-when clauses are each shown by a named test at the committed head.
justifications.reuse: it does not re-implement recovery: the claim release, error count, backoff and retry are the pre-existing scan_worker error path, and the tests drive the real worker through monkeypatched graph_ops rather than a shadow harness. It diverges however from paths/scanner.py's finer distinction (255 transient vs other exits recorded as path errors) by raising on all CalledProcessError.
justifications.scope_discipline: the diff stays inside the declared product write scope (scanner.py, the new test file) across all four commits and adds no unrelated edits; the reviewed scope additionally declared a docs fragment html and a figures directory, neither of which the run produced (finding 1), so the declared scope over-states what was touched rather than the work exceeding it.
